newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat urges Clinton to give peace a "quick push".
newsitem.headline: Arafat urges Clinton to give peace a "quick push".

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat urgently appealed to re-elected U.S. President Bill Clinton on Wednesday to devote himself to saving Middle East peace.
"There must be a quick push from His Excellency so that the peace process will go on the same track," Arafat told the U.S. television network CNN in an interview.

If Clinton did not act swiftly, Arafat said, "we will face some troubles and it will be a good opportunity for the extremists on the two sides -- on our side and on the Israeli side -- to sabotage more and more the peace process."

Teams representing Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Arafat are locked in negotiations on a long-delayed Israeli handover of parts of the West Bank town of Hebron to Palestinian self-rule.
"As you know we are facing a real impasse," Arafat told CNN. Arafat said that while Clinton would have more leverage in his second term, he did not expect the U.S. president to pressure Netanyahu.
"I am not saying pressure, I am saying efforts, to make his effort," Arafat said.
Netanyahu said on Wednesday that he did not expect the Clinton administration to pressure Israel into Making peace concessions.
Earlier Arafat told reporters in the West Bank town of Ramallah: "I am very happy for the victory of a friend of the Palestinian people and a friend of peace".
"I congratulate him and congratulate myself, the Palestinian people and the Arab nation for this victory which will bring stability and give a push to the peace process," Arafat said.
Senior PLO officials expressed the hope that Washington would move Middle East peace talks forward, acting as a referee and being more forceful.
U.S.-sponsored Israeli-PLO talks are deadlocked over implementation of the troop pullback in Hebron, home to 400 Jewish settlers and 100,000 Palestinians.
Palestinians accuse Israel of trying to renegotiate the Hebron deal signed by Israel's previous centre-left government.

Israel was due to redeploy in Hebron last March. The pullback was put on hold after suicide bombings that killed 59 people in Israel in February and March. Netanyahu says he wants to boost security for Jews in Hebron.
Israel's right-wing government has charged Palestinians were delaying a deal until after the American elections in the hopes of increasing U.S. pressure on the Jewish state.
